newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen mired in narrow range in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen mired in narrow range in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be trapped in a narrow range against the yen on Monday in Asia ahead of the release of U.S. and Japanese trade data later this week and the G7 meeting starting on Friday, dealers said.

Given a lack of market-moving factors during the day, the dollar should be relatively stable, with its top limited at around 115.10/20 yen due to persistent selling interest by Japanese exporters and investors, said a trust bank dealer.
"We see offers at above 115.00 yen," he added.
But downside could be also be limited at 114.20 yen as worries about U.S.-Japan trade friction have receded, he said.
The trust bank dealer said the dollar was likely to edge higher versus the yen this week after sharp falls last week.

However, a dealer at a city bank said that if Japanese and U.S. trade data show a large increase in Japan's trade surplus and this rekindles concerns about trade friction between the two nations, the dollar could be sold again against the yen.
Japan's May customs-cleared trade data is due out on Wednesday and U.S. April international trade data on Thursday.
Expectations that Europe's planned single currency will be launced on time, but weaker than previously thought, could support the dollar against the mark, dealers said.
